findings.message: A hand-made container-2 checkpoint that carries supported `matchModel`/`npcSeason` passes `decode` and can be activated as the writer. After that, every commit's `encode` throws `checkpointSchemaFor`'s plain Error (no typed error code), so the career cannot be saved, and no test covers that commit path. Real saves cannot reach this while activation is off, but consider refusing such worlds at activation (or giving the write failure an actionable error) until T282 adds container 3. If you keep the current behaviour, note it as T282's handoff.

`npcSeasonSchema` leaves the club `xg`/`xga` integers without an upper bound, while every other count in the schema is bounded. Bounding them (e.g., the `count` cap in match-model.ts) keeps the strict schema consistent before T280/T281 start writing aggregates.

A `sub` incident with no `other` reports `undefined comes on … as a starter or a second time`, which hides the real fault (a missing incoming player). incidentIssues already flags it as `names undefined outside side`, so this second message is noise. Give the missing-`other` case its own message.

reviewHistory.summary: T273 adds the DTOs, revision, container constant, frame-time checks and a shared validator, and the baseline was captured on the clean base 9f69553. The code is well scoped, but two acceptance claims are not met in practice. First, no load or protocol path rejects future model metadata: validateWorld's non-strict world schema silently drops the new fields, and no remaining task in the group owns schema.ts. Second, the shared validateFullMatchRecord does not tie participation to the substitution timeline, which MATCH-27 requires. Tests could not be re-run here because the review checkout has no node_modules.

findings.message: Acceptance 3 and 6 are checked [v], but assertMatchModelFormat is not called anywhere a save is read. validateWorld (schema.ts:1158) runs only assertIdentityFormatVersions, and worldSchema is a plain z.object (schema.ts:776), so it strips unknown keys. Repro: a container-2 checkpoint world with matchModel.revision 'continuous-aggregate-2' (or ownMatches[i].model set to it) loads through persistence.ts:150 with the metadata silently dropped instead of failing with SaveCompatibilityError, and the next commit rewrites the save without it. SAVE-23 requires a refusal, not silently dropped fields. Supported matchModel/npcSeason/MatchRecord.model would be stripped the same way once T281/T282 write them. Similarly, host.ts:300 still builds { id, revision } itself, so worldMetadataOf is never used at runtime. No remaining group task (T274–T286) lists schema.ts in its touches. Fix: make worldSchema/match accept matchModel (matchModelStateSchema), npcSeason and model (z.enum(MATCH_MODEL_REVISIONS)), call assertMatchModelFormat in validateWorld and beside assertIdentityFormatVersions in persistence.ts:123, and add a load test with a future revision. If touches cannot widen, hand this explicitly to the planner (add schema.ts and persistence wiring to T282, host.ts wiring to T286) and leave acceptance 3/6 unchecked until then.

MATCH-27 and the contract doc say the shared validator checks substitutions sharing the roster and timeline, and time legality. It does not. A side can have 12–16 lines with no 'sub' incident and still pass, because only lines ≤ 11 + maxSubs and the 11×length minute total are checked. A sub's `other` can be a player already on the pitch or a starter. Line minutes are never compared with the incident minutes (a starter replaced at 30′ credited 90 minutes, or a substitute entering at 80′ credited 60, both pass). The limits note says intervals cannot be checked because records lack per-event times, but sub and red-card incidents carry minutes, so every line's on-pitch interval is derivable. T280's aggregate participation relies on this validator, so these gaps would let incoherent aggregate records settle. Fix: per side, require lines = 11 + sub incidents; each incoming `other` must be distinct, not a starter and not already on; minutes for starters, subs and dismissed players must match the incident timeline within the documented added-time rounding. Add the corresponding cases to 'rejects impossible participation and contribution sums'.

validateFullMatchRecord re-implements the existing detailConsistent invariants but leaves some out: finalThirdPasses ≤ passes, progressivePasses ≤ completed passes, buildUpPasses ≤ passes, PD.xg ≤ 80×shots, PD.xa ≤ 80×keyPasses. A full record can pass the shared validator and still be refused by validateWorld as an own match. Share one invariant helper, or at least cover the existing set, so the two checks cannot drift.

The baseline ran its century profiles at 20 seasons instead of the configured release 100, and the provisionalReason was hand-edited in the JSON while scripts/match-model-baseline.ts still emits the stale pre-T255 string. It is honestly marked provisional/releaseEvidence:false. However, T285 says it compares with 'T273's captured baseline', and T286 does not explicitly re-run the baseline source for 100 seasons. Planner handoff: state in T285/T286 that the paired release run re-executes source 9f69553 with --seasons 100 on the same machine, and fix the runner's reason string in the task that owns the script.

The limits note says 3 of the 600 current grid pilot records have a side's minutes at 991 > 990. These records would fail assertFullMatchRecord once grid records carry the model. No downstream task's acceptance names this rounding fix. Hand it to the planner so T274 (or whichever task first tags grid records with the model) owns it, rather than loosening the check.

dispatch.summary: T274 meets its acceptance. The change is large (1,246 lines, 13 files, all inside touches), so I checked the risky parts first. Without model metadata the old path is unchanged: I ran 12 fixtures (2024/1966/1950/2010, some knockout ties, half of them observed) on baseCommit d7742d5 and on beb6b9e from extracted copies, and the records, elapsed time, diagnostics and serialised traces hash identically. I also ran 60 candidate fixtures of my own (five eras including 1990, a third of them knockout ties). All 60 pass validateFullMatchRecord, and observed and unobserved runs settle identical records and elapsed time. Knots are in time order. Between consecutive trace entries in a period, no player moves faster than top speed; the only exceptions are the explicit substitution entries at benchPoint. GRID_MOVEMENT_CONFIG and GRID_BALL_CONFIG use the contract defaults (4/6 m/s², 180°/s; ball speeds 20/20/18/30/40). The retrieval (6 m/s) and placement (1.5 s) values are additions, and they are documented in the contract. Each restart is prepared once on the clock: dead time is the larger of the nominal value and what the preparation actually needs. Added-time credits come from the dead seconds actually charged, the wait beyond nominal is credited once, and the engine test confirms that dead time plus ball-in-play equals elapsed. lineMinutes rounds each entry/exit boundary once and keeps them in order, which fixes the 991 > 990 case without loosening the validator. The five named movement tests and the engine transition tests are present and meaningful. Band drift and the 1.9× cost are recorded for T278 and T285; renderer pacing is left to T275, which already owns knot playback. Only minor optional findings remain. The 'autopilot decisions awaiting the owner' risk refers to upstream planning decisions, not to anything T274 decided beyond what the contract allows.

findings.message: After `advance`, prepareRestart always sets `gp.pos = spot`. If `reachSeconds` ever stops at `GRID_MOVEMENT_CONFIG.horizon` (300 s) without arriving, the taker would jump to the spot silently instead of the gap being noticed. This never happened in 60 candidate fixtures I checked for continuity. Consider asserting or capping explicitly, so a missed arrival shows up instead of being placed (useful when T278 tunes the config).

The candidate branch repeats the jitter `secondsOf(played.key) * (0.85 + 0.3 * r())` that the pre-feature branch draws a few lines below. A shared helper or named constant would stop the two duration draws from drifting apart when T278 retunes them. Optional.

The candidate path overwrites the substitute's position with benchPoint after changes.ts has copied the outgoing player's position (limit 4). This is correct as an explicit 'entry' transition. Moving the touchline entry point into changes.ts (outside T274's touches) would leave one owner for substitute placement, a natural cleanup for T276, which owns the 'unavailable/exit' part of the intention lifecycle.

findings.message: restartTaken() gives the players in scene.up a committed `run`/`box` intention until s.elapsed + SHAPE_CONFIG.setPiece.stay (8 s), replacing holdSetPiece. However, prepareRestart() has already advanced every scene player onto that exact spot (seconds ≥ reachSeconds for each placement). The first updateIntentions() after the kick (engine.ts ~679) then reaches verdict(): case 'run' only checks possession and falls through to the generic `gap(gp.pos, i.target) <= C.arrive → 'arrival'`. So every box holder's intention ends 'arrival' at the kick, endIntention clears gp.run, and targetOf sends him back to shape or a fresh tactical choice. The 'hold box spots for 8 s for the second ball' behavior stated in MATCH-ENGINE-DESIGN §4.5 and the T276 result is effectively 0 s, a regression against T274's candidate path, where holdSetPiece kept gp.run for the full stay. Fix: make a held box run (committed `run: 'box'`), or more generally any hold-type intention, end only on expiry, turnover or a higher priority, not on arrival. Add a regression test in intentions.test.ts. Example: after a candidate corner or free kick that stays in possession, scene.up players keep their box intention, and targetOf returns the spot until setPiece.stay, unless there is a turnover. Rerun the set-piece measurements recorded for T278 (set-piece goals 19.2% is already out of band).

Still open from the prior review. Substitution, injury and dismissal endings and restart intentions never appear in TraceEntry.intentions. The leaver is off the pitch (or his slot is refilled) before the snapshot, and restart intentions start and end inside the prepareRestart callback. Engine state records them, but playback and the inspector cannot show these reasons. Either trace the leaver's ended intention on his exit or entry note, or record this as a limit handed to T275/T277.

losePass() synthesizes a receive intention, then ends it as 'lost'. setIntention first ends the receiver's real intention (e.g. a run) as 'replaced', and the synthetic record then overwrites GridPlayer.ended, so the real ending is lost. Similarly, carryTo() ends the carrier's just-achieved receive as 'replaced' (displaced) rather than 'arrival'. When danger starts while a tactical presser already holds the carrier, `urgent = danger && pressing.length === 0` is false. No presser takes danger priority, and the existing one stays tactical: line-bound and dropped at 1.6 × reach. The design doc says the first presser takes danger priority in danger. Either escalate the existing first presser or adjust the doc; otherwise hand this to T277's side-level assignment.

reviewHistory.summary: T280 correction 7e7cb9f6 (d32b4256 on be7efe89): the per-side streams do stop the mirroring. I checked independently on new founding worlds. With the repo's FNV-1a → xorshift32 PRNG, two seeds that differ only in their last character produce strongly correlated draws. The first uniform each side draws correlates at 0.32, the Poisson card counts at 0.23, and home and away yellow counts across world matches at 0.27. The new test checks only for identical minute lists, so it cannot see this. findings.message: T280 / ARCH-5, MATCH-21, CLUB-23: sideDraw builds `${streams.names(family, period)}:side${side}`, so the two sides' seeds differ only in their final character ('0' vs '1'). primitives.ts `random` seeds xorshift32 straight from FNV-1a with no warm-up. A last-character difference therefore leaves the two states a fixed multiple of the FNV prime apart, and their outputs are correlated. Measured on 20,000 fixtures (aggregateStreams + sideDraw, 'discipline', regulation): the correlation of side 0's and side 1's first uniform is 0.325, 0.093 at the second draw and 0.078 at the sixth; for poissonDraw(r, 1.9), the first draw of the card count, it is 0.226. Two unrelated names give 0.001. In the world (seed probe-r3a, 2,000 of 2024 via playAggregate/aggregateRecord) the correlation of home and away yellow counts is 0.272, and 0.266 in 1990. The same coupling hits each line's first injury uniform (hurtDraws), the changes jitter and the per-side attribution streams in players.ts:383. So the sides are no longer copies, but their cards, injuries and stoppages still move together, which will distort T284's distributions. Fix: put the side component ahead of the remaining name characters, e.g. `<seed>:<rev>:aggregate:<family>:side<n>[:<period>]:<fixture>`. Measured with the same probe, that gives a correlation of 0.000 on the first draw and 0.011 on the second. Alternatively, mix the seed so that suffixes decorrelate. Add a regression test on the correlation of home/away first draws or card counts over a large sample (e.g. |r| < 0.05), not just on identical minute lists, then re-measure the card, injury, rebalance and retry figures in the result.

T280 (handoff, outside touches): the same weakness exists before this commit for any two stream names that differ only at the end, including fixture IDs that differ in their last character. For example `...:regulation:ENG:0:<i>:3:0` vs `...:3:1` correlate at 0.323 on the first draw. This is a PRNG-seeding concern for ARCH-5 across every system that puts the fixture or entity ID last. It belongs to a separate task (e.g. a seed mixing step with portable test vectors) and should not be fixed inside T280. Record it for the planner or T284.

Before T277, the mark loop ran after the press was set and picked a replacement in the same update. Suggested fix: don't add the runner to `marked` (or put him back into pairing) when his current marker is already in `claimed` for another job. Add a danger-scenario test for this.

MATCH-27 and the contract doc say the shared validator checks substitutions sharing the roster and timeline, and time legality. It does not. A side can have 12–16 lines with no 'sub' incident and still pass, because only lines ≤ 11 + maxSubs and the 11×length minute total are checked. A sub's `other` can be a player already on the pitch or a starter. Line minutes are never compared with the incident minutes (a starter replaced at 30′ credited 90 minutes, or a substitute entering at 80′ credited 60, both pass). The limits note says intervals cannot be checked because records lack per-event times, but sub and red-card incidents carry minutes, so every line's on-pitch interval is derivable. T280's aggregate participation relies on this validator, so these gaps would let incoherent aggregate records settle. Fix: per side, require lines = 11 + sub incidents; each incoming `other` must be distinct, not a starter and not already on; minutes for starters, subs and dismissed players must match the incident timeline within the documented added-time rounding. Add the corresponding cases to 'rejects impossible participation and contribution sums'.

validateFullMatchRecord re-implements the existing detailConsistent invariants but leaves some out: finalThirdPasses ≤ passes, progressivePasses ≤ completed passes, buildUpPasses ≤ passes, PD.xg ≤ 80×shots, PD.xa ≤ 80×keyPasses. A full record can pass the shared validator and still be refused by validateWorld as an own match. Share one invariant helper, or at least cover the existing set, so the two checks cannot drift.

- **지적 2 (교체 타임라인):** `validateFullMatchRecord`가 이제 선수 출전을 교체·퇴장 기록과 맞춰 봅니다.

  - 모든 사건(카드·교체·부상)은 그 순간 경기장에 있는 선수를 가리켜야 합니다. 부상으로 나간 선수의 교체는 허용합니다.
  - 교체 투입 선수는 한 번만, 선발이 아닌 선수만 들어올 수 있습니다.
  - 각 선수의 출전 분은 투입~퇴장 구간과 ±2분 안에서 맞아야 합니다. 이 오차는 grid/changes.test.ts에 이미 문서화된 반올림 폭입니다.
- **지적 3 (기존 저장 스키마 경계):** 저장 스키마가 이미 거는 경계를 검증기에도 넣었습니다(파이널서드·빌드업 패스 ≤ 패스, 전진 패스 ≤ 성공 패스, 선수 xG ≤ 슈팅×0.80, xA ≤ 키패스×0.80). 다만 schema.ts의 원본 함수가 범위 밖이고 export되지 않아 공용 함수로 합치지는 못했습니다.
- 테스트(15개)와 계약 문서·저장 형식 문서도 갱신했습니다.

- **지적 4:** T285·T286에 '짝 비교 때 9f69553 소스를 `--seasons 100`으로 같은 기계에서 다시 측정한다'를 명시하고, 실행기의 낡은 provisionalReason 문구를 고칠 태스크를 정해야 합니다.

I reviewed T273 at dae3d0b against 9fa8360. The two P2 findings from correction 3525e61e are fixed.

(1) Load path. `validateWorld` and `readCheckpoint` now run `assertMatchModelFormat` before unpacking or Zod parsing. The world and match schemas keep supported `matchModel` (strict), `npcSeason` (strict, its shape matches `NpcSeasonStats`) and record `model`. The host answers metadata-only inspections with `worldMetadataOf`. Tests cover a future revision as a `SaveCompatibilityError` in containers 1 and 2, the check running before damaged packing is detected, malformed data as an ordinary error, and the host refusing without activating the world. `checkpointSchemaFor` keeps unactivated worlds writing container 2 and refuses to write model data until T282 adds container 3, which satisfies SAVE-23's rule that data must not be silently dropped.

(2) MATCH-27 timeline. Each side now has exactly 11 lines plus one per substitution, and the substitutes appear in the order they came on. An incoming player cannot be a starter or come on twice. Every incident must name a player on the pitch. Each line's minutes must match its entry–exit interval within 2 minutes; I checked this against the grid, where an injured player leaves at once and red cards and substitutions both call `leave`. With the line count tied to substitutions, removing the old `11 + maxSubs` line cap loses nothing, because the substitution count is still limited to the era's maximum. P3 finding 3 is covered (the counter bounds), and the planner reassigned P3 findings 4 and 5 in 9fa8360 (STATE inbox, T274/T285/T286). The risk entry about files outside `touches` is out of date: base 9fa8360 adds persistence, host, schema and their tests to the touches list.

I could not re-run the tests: the review checkout has no node_modules, and I did not want to use another checkout. The worker reports typecheck, lint, format:check and build passing, plus 129 targeted tests and a wider affected set of 422 tests. The full changed-file run and the unit/contract suites are still left to the runner. Only minor improvements remain.

findings.message: A hand-made container-2 checkpoint that carries supported `matchModel`/`npcSeason` passes `decode` and can be activated as the writer. After that, every commit's `encode` throws `checkpointSchemaFor`'s plain Error (no typed error code), so the career cannot be saved, and no test covers that commit path. Real saves cannot reach this while activation is off, but consider refusing such worlds at activation (or giving the write failure an actionable error) until T282 adds container 3. If you keep the current behaviour, note it as T282's handoff.

`npcSeasonSchema` leaves the club `xg`/`xga` integers without an upper bound, while every other count in the schema is bounded. Bounding them (e.g., the `count` cap in match-model.ts) keeps the strict schema consistent before T280/T281 start writing aggregates.

A `sub` incident with no `other` reports `undefined comes on … as a starter or a second time`, which hides the real fault (a missing incoming player). incidentIssues already flags it as `names undefined outside side`, so this second message is noise. Give the missing-`other` case its own message.

dispatch.summary:
T276 is implemented. On the candidate match model, every player now holds a persistent intention, defined in the new `grid/intentions.ts`. The old path (no model set) is unchanged, so production is untouched: the release switch is still off.

**What an intention is**
- It has a kind, a priority (exit > restart > danger > committed > tactical), a target, an optional teammate or opponent, a start time and an expiry.
- The last intention that ended is kept with its ending and its reason (`INTENTION_REASONS`).
- Ordinary updates keep any intention that is still feasible. It ends on arrival, expiry, being unreachable, the carrier moving on, a lost pass, or a referenced player leaving. It is displaced by a higher priority, a turnover, an urgent danger, a restart, a substitution, an injury or a sending-off. When a player leaves, every intention that points at him ends.
- Runs are now intentions. `GridPlayer.run` remains as a view of them. The old run starter and the new code share one `runPlan`, so there is no second planner.

**How players choose**
- Role and play-trait weights choose who presses, covers and runs.
- 판단력 affects run timing, how soon a player recovers and which side he shows on; 침착성 affects whether he shows for a pressured carrier.
- Fatigue (minutes played and 체력) lowers the odds of runs and pressing.
- Random draws are keyed by fixture, decision, player and moment, never by the match stream or update order.

**Engine, trace and playback**
- Intentions update once per action, after it is applied and before anyone moves. The first version updated after movement: pressers chased the passer while the ball was in flight, which lowered tackles + interceptions to about 21 and raised goals to about 3.5.
- Trace entries carry each slot's intention, the target the movement actually used, and a motion state taken from the intention. Playback attaches the intention to each player, with partners named by player ID.
- Design doc §4.5 and §10 are updated.

review.summary:
T276 meets its acceptance criteria. I checked the two risk reasons first. The large diff (1304 lines) stays inside the task's touches. The autopilot decisions waiting for the owner are group-level base raises; this task adds no new SSOT decision. intentions.ts implements the contract's lifecycle with a reason map to achieved/expired/infeasible/displaced. Its priority order is exit > restart > danger > committed > tactical. Runs go through the shared runPlan, so there is no second planner. The engine hooks cover turnover, restart, lost passes, substitution, injury and dismissal, and depart() clears references by roster index. Each trace entry carries the slot's intention, with targets matching the ones movement uses, and playback exposes them as IntentionObservation with player-ID partners. Calibration drift is recorded for T278, the extra fixture time for T285, and carrier use in decide.ts for T277, which owns it.

I re-checked this independently rather than relying only on the worker's run. On base and head source trees exported to a scratch directory, the pre-feature path gave an identical SHA-256 hash over 96 matches (16 tactic pairings × 3 fixtures, observed and unobserved), covering records, elapsed time, positions, targets and states. On 32 candidate matches, observed and unobserved runs settled identical records. Every record passed validateFullMatchRecord. No held intention referenced an off-pitch player, and goalkeepers held only receive/carry. intentions.test.ts and shape.test.ts passed (18/18). The findings below are optional improvements only.

findings.message: Exit and restart intentions never reach the trace. A player who leaves (substitution, injury or dismissal) is skipped by snapshot() once he is off the pitch, and his slot now holds the substitute. Restart intentions start and end inside the preparer, between two trace entries. Across 32 candidate matches I measured zero traced substitution/injury/dismissal endings and zero held restart intentions. The engine still records them on GridPlayer.ended, so the acceptance is met, but playback and the inspector cannot show these reasons. Consider tracing the leaver's ended intention on his exit note, or recording this as a limit for T275/T277.

A receiver only commits to receiving after he owns the ball, so losePass() creates a receive intention and ends it as 'lost' straight away. If the intended receiver was on a run, setIntention first ends the run as 'replaced', and the synthetic 'lost' record then overwrites GridPlayer.ended, so the run's real ending is never recorded. Consider ending the existing intention directly as 'lost'. Alternatively, committing the receiver when the pass is played would make the lifecycle real rather than reconstructed.

In danger, free(gp, 'danger') lets a player who is tactically marking runner A be reassigned to mark runner B, leaving A unmarked until the next update. This is a coordination gap that T277's side-level assignment should close; mention it in the hand-off so it is not lost.

findings.message: Exit and restart intentions never reach the trace. A player who leaves (substitution, injury or dismissal) is skipped by snapshot() once he is off the pitch, and his slot now holds the substitute. Restart intentions start and end inside the preparer, between two trace entries. Across 32 candidate matches I measured zero traced substitution/injury/dismissal endings and zero held restart intentions. The engine still records them on GridPlayer.ended, so the acceptance is met, but playback and the inspector cannot show these reasons. Consider tracing the leaver's ended intention on his exit note, or recording this as a limit for T275/T277.

A receiver only commits to receiving after he owns the ball, so losePass() creates a receive intention and ends it as 'lost' straight away. If the intended receiver was on a run, setIntention first ends the run as 'replaced', and the synthetic 'lost' record then overwrites GridPlayer.ended, so the run's real ending is never recorded. Consider ending the existing intention directly as 'lost'. Alternatively, committing the receiver when the pass is played would make the lifecycle real rather than reconstructed.

In danger, free(gp, 'danger') lets a player who is tactically marking runner A be reassigned to mark runner B, leaving A unmarked until the next update. This is a coordination gap that T277's side-level assignment should close; mention it in the hand-off so it is not lost.

I fixed the P2 regression from correction 52f9a9dc and handled all three P3 notes.

**P2: box hold after set pieces.** Players who went up for a set piece now hold their box spot for the full 8 s again (`setPiece.stay`). Their hold was ending as "arrived" at the kick, because they were already standing on the spot. Now a held box run never ends on arrival, only at expiry, on a turnover or by a higher priority.
- A new regression test checks that `targetOf` returns the spot for every second up to the stay, that the hold ends at the stay or on a turnover, and that in played matches it never ends on arrival.

**P3 fixes:**
- **Lost pass:** the run a player was played into now ends as `lost` and keeps its own record. Before, a fake receive overwrote it. A player with no intention gets a zero-length receive from the passer, ended `lost`.
- **Carry after a reception:** the reception the carrier reached now ends as `arrival`, not `replaced`.
- **Danger escalation:** a presser already on the carrier when danger starts is raised to danger priority and keeps the same intention.
- **Traced exits:** exit and entry notes now carry `TraceEntry.left`, the leaver's ended intention with its reason (substitution, injury, sending-off). Restart intentions still never show in the traced slots; I recorded that as a limit for T275.

The design doc (§4.5 and the trace section) and the task result are updated.

**Checks:** typecheck, lint and format pass. `vitest --changed fffc9ae` ran in 6 shards (one shell call is capped at 10 minutes): 196 files, 1,340 tests passed, 4 skipped, including all 7 tests in `intentions.test.ts`.

- Set-piece goals rose from 19.2% to 20.1%, now inside the band. Headed goals rose to 20.8%, now 0.8 points above it.
- Goals 2.74, tackles + interceptions 25.7.

findings.message: T280 / STAFF-45, MATCH-20, MATCH-27: STAFF-45 says a red card makes any manager rebalance at the next stoppage when the side is down to ten and level or ahead, so the change is required, not just allowed. settleParticipation adds every red that trailed in some replay to `withheld` and never takes it back. But generateTeamFacts draws whole-period facts from sideUnits over [0,90), so withholding the change at minute m moves the goals before m as well. How it was reproduced: an isolated copy at 3bc2a92b, simulateAggregate on 3,000 founding-world fixtures from the engine.test.ts `others()` pool with year 2024. For each withheld key, re-plan without that key to find its stoppage minute, then check scoreBefore on the settled facts. Result: 93 withheld keys, 149 rebalances kept, and in 20 cases the settled record shows the side level or ahead at that very stoppage (e.g. '1:1 m=87 score +2', '0:2 m=67 level') with no rebalance. A settled record should not break STAFF-45 in either direction. The task result's limit (0) reports 14 of these but treats a missing rebalance as acceptable. Fix options: (a) make the score before a stoppage independent of the decision taken at it, e.g. generate facts causally up to the stoppage as the previous review suggested, or at least re-admit a withheld rebalance whose settled score is level or ahead; (b) if no consistent fixed point exists on the same streams, settle it with a deterministic, documented tie-break. Either way, extend 'makes no red-card rebalance while trailing' (participation.test.ts:169) to check that every withheld red trails at its stoppage in the settled facts. Run that check on world fixtures (simulateAggregate with year 2024), because the synthetic 2008 fixtures never trigger the case. If this residual is judged acceptable, it needs a planning decision (update-ssot or a STATE inbox entry recording that the aggregate path may leave a level or ahead rebalance unmade). It should not stay only as a worker limit.

T280: once a red's key is withheld, the planner never offers that rebalance again. The grid retries at every later stoppage (grid/changes.ts:184, `c.reds > c.rebalanced && score >= 0`), so it rebalances once a trailing ten-man side draws level. In the same 3,000-fixture probe, 10 withheld reds belonged to sides that were level or ahead at a later substitution stoppage, where the grid would have made the change. STAFF-45's wording ('at the next stoppage') arguably allows this, but the two engines now differ. Align them while fixing the P2, or note the difference for T281/T286.

review.summary: T277 meets its acceptance criteria and the design requirements for coordinated play (MATCH-16/17). The new grid/coordination.ts plans every job for both sides from one snapshot without changing the state, and applyCoordination gives the jobs out. Each player gets at most one job, and equal costs break by player ID. Handovers are explicit: the marker's record ends as achieved/handover and names the teammate who took over. In decide.ts, the carrier's choice reads only teammates' actual show and overlap intentions, so the pre-feature path is unchanged. On risk: the 1414-line diff is mostly tests plus code moved out of intentions.ts. The move is behaviour-preserving: INTENTION_CONFIG's support/mark/cover/recover values moved to COORDINATION_CONFIG with no leftover readers, and the split into targetOf + shapePlace keeps the old GK/run order. Every changed file is within touches, and no probability overrides were added; band gaps are handed to T278. The tests cover all nine required scenarios with compact fixtures. I did not rerun them because this checkout has no node_modules; the worker's record says typecheck, lint, format and the changed-file vitest run passed. The autopilot decision awaiting the owner is the group-level base raise in STATE, which does not affect T277's content. Two minor issues, neither blocking.

findings.message: T277: In defend(), a runner counts as marked whenever someone currently marks him, even if the plan has just taken that marker for an urgent danger press. Applying the press then ends the mark, so the runner has no marker until the next update. That one action is exactly when a through ball to him is dangerous. Before T277, the mark loop ran after the press was set and picked a replacement in the same update. Suggested fix: don't add the runner to `marked` (or put him back into pairing) when his current marker is already in `claimed` for another job. Add a danger-scenario test for this.

T277: Lane clearance doesn't check for an existing `support: 'open'` intention for the carrier. If a show ends as `closed` while its clearance is still running, a new show can be planned and a second teammate assigned to clear its lane. That breaks §4.6's 'Only one teammate shows and one clears per carrier'. Rare, but easy to guard: skip the clearance when a teammate already holds an 'open' support for this carrier.

findings.message: T275 / MATCH-12: candidate minutes draw only start..start+60, so a period's last action past its final minute is not drawn. A probe of 30 candidate matches found this in 60 of 60 periods, up to 32 s, not just occasionally as the limits imply (no shot or goal fell in the overrun there, but nothing prevents one). At every whistle the ball stops mid-action. The frameTimeIssues 60 s cap (T273 contract, outside T275 touches) forbids drawing it, so the hand-off is legitimate. But T273 is closed and no T286 acceptance item covers it. In 117 extra-time ties regulation was always level. Every record passed validateFullMatchRecord. Repeat calls gave identical records, the targeted vitest passes (7 files, 59 tests) and production paths are untouched. The same probe exposed a correctness defect that earlier rounds missed. planParticipation's two SidePlanners open the same named discipline, injury and change streams, so both sides draw identical sequences. Their cards, injuries and stoppage times mirror each other.

findings.message: T280 / MATCH-4, MATCH-21, CLUB-23, ARCH-5: SidePlanner.playPeriod calls streams.draw('discipline'|'injuries'|'changes', period) for each side, and planParticipation (participation.ts:740) runs both sides on the same AggregateStreams. aggregateStreams.draw (team.ts:45) restarts random(name) from a name with no side in it, so home and away get the same uniform sequence. Measured on 1,000 founding-world 2024 fixtures (simulateAggregate): in 647 of the 852 matches with yellows, both sides were booked at exactly the same minutes; in 31 of the 49 matches with a dismissal, both sides lost a player in the same minute (e.g. ENG:0:0:3:8 at :probe:38, a secondYellow for slot 9 on both sides at 27'); in 98 of the 229 matches with injuries, both sides had one in the same minute. Changes jitter is shared too, so stoppage minutes coincide. Each side needs its own named streams, e.g. a side component in the stream name (discipline:<side>:<period>), so that one side's draws neither copy the other's nor move when the other side draws more. Add a test that both sides' card, injury and stoppage minutes are not identical across a world sample, and re-measure the yellow, red and injury rates and the rebalance and retry figures afterwards.

T280: if no search reconciles the red-card answers within rebalanceRetries, playAggregate throws. Nothing in production calls it yet, and I saw nothing beyond retry 1 in 5,000 matches. Once T281 dispatches season fixtures here, though, the throw would abort a whole season simulation. Hand the fallback (or a documented deterministic tie-break) to T281 or T284 together with the retry-bias measurement.

reviewHistory.summary: T280 correction 7e7cb9f6 (d32b4256 on be7efe89): the per-side streams do stop the mirroring. I checked independently on new founding worlds. Seed probe-r3a, 2,000 matches of 2024: the two sides had identical yellow minutes in 6 of 1,474 matches where both were booked, a red in the same minute in 0 of 5, and an injury in the same minute in 1 of 88. Rates were 3.85 yellows, 0.113 reds, 0.47 injuries and 10.00 substitutions a match. Rebalances: 106 made, 50 withheld, 0 disagreeing with the settled score, 10 settled on retry 1, every record valid. Seed probe-r3b, 1,000 matches of 1990, gave similar results. The targeted vitest also passes (6 files, 57 tests). The fix still leaves the two sides' streams correlated, though. `sideDraw` adds `:side<n>` as the last characters of the stream name. With the repo's FNV-1a → xorshift32 PRNG, two seeds that differ only in their last character produce strongly correlated draws. The first uniform each side draws correlates at 0.32, the Poisson card counts at 0.23, and home and away yellow counts across world matches at 0.27. The new test checks only for identical minute lists, so it cannot see this. The earlier rounds' P3 (the throw once rebalanceRetries runs out) is now handed to T281/T284 in the task's limits, which is acceptable.

findings.message: T280 / ARCH-5, MATCH-21, CLUB-23: sideDraw builds `${streams.names(family, period)}:side${side}`, so the two sides' seeds differ only in their final character ('0' vs '1'). primitives.ts `random` seeds xorshift32 straight from FNV-1a with no warm-up. A last-character difference therefore leaves the two states a fixed multiple of the FNV prime apart, and their outputs are correlated. Measured on 20,000 fixtures (aggregateStreams + sideDraw, 'discipline', regulation): the correlation of side 0's and side 1's first uniform is 0.325, 0.093 at the second draw and 0.078 at the sixth; for poissonDraw(r, 1.9), the first draw of the card count, it is 0.226. Two unrelated names give 0.001. In the world (seed probe-r3a, 2,000 of 2024 via playAggregate/aggregateRecord) the correlation of home and away yellow counts is 0.272, and 0.266 in 1990. The same coupling hits each line's first injury uniform (hurtDraws), the changes jitter and the per-side attribution streams in players.ts:383. So the sides are no longer copies, but their cards, injuries and stoppages still move together, which will distort T284's distributions. Fix: put the side component ahead of the remaining name characters, e.g. `<seed>:<rev>:aggregate:<family>:side<n>[:<period>]:<fixture>`. Measured with the same probe, that gives a correlation of 0.000 on the first draw and 0.011 on the second. Alternatively, mix the seed so that suffixes decorrelate. Add a regression test on the correlation of home/away first draws or card counts over a large sample (e.g. |r| < 0.05), not just on identical minute lists, then re-measure the card, injury, rebalance and retry figures in the result.

T280 (handoff, outside touches): the same weakness exists before this commit for any two stream names that differ only at the end, including fixture IDs that differ in their last character. For example `...:regulation:ENG:0:<i>:3:0` vs `...:3:1` correlate at 0.323 on the first draw. This is a PRNG-seeding concern for ARCH-5 across every system that puts the fixture or entity ID last. It belongs to a separate task (e.g. a seed mixing step with portable test vectors) and should not be fixed inside T280. Record it for the planner or T284.

dispatch.summary: Fixed review e77389d7 for T280. P2: the side marker sat at the end of each stream name, and the seed hash leaves names that differ only in their last characters correlated: the two sides' first draws correlated at 0.33. `sideDraw` now builds `…:aggregate:<family>:side<n>[:<period>]:<fixture>` through `streams.draw`, so the period and fixture still follow the side; team.ts is untouched. On 20,000 fixtures the first-draw correlation dropped to 0.011. A new test, 'keeps the two sides' streams uncorrelated', draws 10,000 names for each of the four side streams (discipline, injuries, changes, attribution) and requires |r| < 0.05 for the first and second draws and a Poisson card count; the old naming fails it at 0.33. Re-measured on founding-world fixtures (a quarter as cup ties): home/away yellow-count correlation 0.013 (3,000 of 2024), 0.016 (2,000 of 2024, seed probe-r3a) and 0.050 (2,000 of 1990, seed probe-r3b, about 2 standard errors), against the reviewer's 0.272 and 0.266. Injury-count correlations were between −0.007 and 0.037. Yellows per match 3.73–3.84, reds 0.086–0.116, injuries 0.48–0.51. Rebalances: 155/70, 86/44 and 86/40 made/withheld, 0 disagreeing with the score in any sample; 0.3–0.5% of fixtures needed one retry, none needed two, and every record was valid. P3 is outside this task's files and is written into the result limits for the planner or T284: the PRNG seeding (FNV-1a straight into xorshift32) correlates any two stream names that differ only in their last characters, so it needs a seed-mixing step with portable test vectors. Checks that passed: typecheck, lint, format:check, the aggregate and match-model tests (6 files, 58 tests) and `vitest run --changed d32b4256` (3 files, 36 tests). Full suites, contract tests, catalog validation, the build and the Chromium journeys are left to the batch gate. The result section is four single-line bullets.

review.summary: I approve T280 correction e77389d7 (25bae723 on d32b4256, base 17418943). The previous review's P2 is fixed: the side marker no longer comes last in the stream name. `sideDraw` now passes `<family>:side<n>` through `streams.draw`, so the name reads `…:aggregate:<family>:side<n>[:<period>]:<fixture>`. The period and fixture characters follow the side marker, so the two sides' seeds no longer differ only at the end. I re-ran the repo's FNV-1a → xorshift32 PRNG in plain node, since the review checkout has no node_modules. Setup: seeds synthetic, probe-r4 and a; families discipline, injuries, changes and attribution; periods regulation, extra and none; 20,000 fixtures each. The home/away correlation of the first six uniforms stays within ±0.02, against a standard error of about 0.007. On the new test's exact names (10,000 `ENG:0:i:3:i%10`), the first uniform correlates at 0.007–0.024, the second at ≤0.016 and a Poisson count at ≤0.011. The old suffix naming gives 0.325–0.340 on the same names. The new test `keeps the two sides' streams uncorrelated` uses fixed seeds, so it is deterministic, and it is strong enough to fail the old naming. `gives each side its own named stream` still checks that a side's sequence restarts by name and does not depend on the other side's draws. Both callers of `sideDraw` pick up the new naming: participation.ts:446-448 and players.ts:383. team.ts streams are untouched. The result text is updated with the new figures and correctly marks the earlier rounds' runs as not re-claimed. The general PRNG-seeding weakness stays handed off to the planner/T284 in the task's limits. The delta to the previously reviewed 2,988-line submission is 46 lines in 3 files and opens no new risk. The other risk reasons (rework, autopilot decisions) were covered by earlier rounds and are recorded in the task's limits.

findings.message: T280: `${family}:side${side}` is cast `as AggregateStreamFamily` to get the side into the middle of the name. Behaviour is correct, but the type now claims a value that is not in AGGREGATE_STREAM_FAMILIES, and nothing guards the name layout `sideDraw` relies on if team.ts `names` is ever changed to validate or map families. Optional cleanup: widen `AggregateStreams.names`/`draw` to take an optional stream suffix, or add a typed side-aware name builder in team.ts, so no cast is needed. This is not blocking.

T280 (handoff, same root cause as the e77389d7 P3 already recorded in limits): `<fixture>:retry<n>` places the retry index last, so retry streams n and n+1 differ only in their final character and start correlated, at about 0.32 on the first draw under the current `random` seeding. In practice no fixture has gone past retry 1, so this is not blocking. The planned seed-mixing task (ARCH-5) should cover the retry names too, and T284's retry-bias measurement should take this into account.
